handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For pax8 the manifest gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: PAX8_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both PAX8_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the OAuth client-credentials token endpoint's error body; the token refresh endpoint's error body. The `auth login` token exchange (internal/cli/auth.go mintClientCredentialsToken) funnels its error body with the client secret it sent. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts. pax8 4.34.2 reprint: the token endpoint's error bodies (mint and refresh, both under the token-state lock) are masked through shownTokenErrorBody, a lock-free view of the same masks (rejected-mint-returns).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

Press 4.34.0's client.go.tmpl has no audience support and no spec extension expresses one (first noted on the 4.22 reprint as not absorbed upstream), so a reprint regenerates client.go without it. The install-credentials-declared-on-every-channel entry pins only the PAX8_AUDIENCE declarations in manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md: a reprint that dropped the code would leave PAX8_AUDIENCE declared but unread. check_env_schema.py then fails, but its fix hint ('Drop it everywhere if the binary no longer reads it') steers toward deleting the declarations, which would remove the override for good; this entry instead fails check_handfixes.py at the dropped lines and names the hand edit to restore. These asserts are code_only so a doc comment naming the function cannot satisfy them. pax8 4.34.2 reprint: the shipped `auth login` minted without the audience, so the token it saved was unusable; both mint paths now build their body with client.ClientCredentialsTokenForm (token-request-body-credentials).

handfixes.summary: A client built under --dry-run refuses every request at its transport, so no write, mint or refresh can reach Pax8 whatever a command does with the client; `auth login --dry-run` sends nothing too.
handfixes.why: Defense in depth beside dry-run-never-mints: the generated preview path returns before sending, and this transport makes a missed branch fail closed. The black-box test runs writes and auth login under --dry-run from a cold start against a fake token host and API host and counts zero requests on both.

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (create or update a company or contact, delete a contact, create an order, update or cancel a subscription) returns a preview of the request and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true; the gate wraps every non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so one a later print adds is gated too.
handfixes.why: Work order connector note: every MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. Press 4.34.2's in-process endpoint handlers (makeAPIHandler) send writes directly. The gate (hand file internal/mcp/pax8_endpoint_confirm.go) is installed by one anchored line in the generated tools.go after every registration and before the read-only drop. The black-box test drives the real MCP server against a fake Pax8: no write without confirm, the string "true" previews, and boolean true sends (control).

handfixes.summary: One client_credentials token body for both mint paths (client.ClientCredentialsTokenForm): grant_type, client_id, client_secret and audience in the form body (client_secret_post), optional scope; no HTTP Basic header.
handfixes.why: Pax8's token manager documents the client credentials and the audience in the request body (research brief: POST https://token-manager.pax8.com/oauth/token with grant_type, client_id, client_secret, audience); the published connector sent them that way. Press 4.34.2 moved the credentials to HTTP Basic and builds the form in two places, one of which (`auth login`) never carried the audience. A reprint re-renders both mint functions, so tools/apply_edits.py re-points them at the one builder. TestMintSendsPax8TokenForm failed on the generated code (Basic header, empty client_id/client_secret/audience).

handfixes.summary: A rejected client-credentials mint returns its error instead of hanging: the rendered mint is mintClientCredentialsRaw behind a hand wrapper, and the token endpoint's error bodies are masked through shownTokenErrorBody, a view with its own lock (the ninjaone shape).
handfixes.why: The exchange runs with the token-state lock held and maskCredentialText takes the same non-reentrant lock, so the funnel's masked token-error body deadlocked every rejected mint (jamf-pro and threecx 2026-10-27; ~/printing-press/fleet/bin/mint_lock_scan.py exit 1 on this tree). TestRejectedMintReturnsWithoutTheSecret hung 15 s on the generated code (cold mint and 401 re-mint) and passes now; mint_lock_scan exit 0.

handfixes.summary: doctor treats Pax8's real API root (https://api.pax8.com/v1, the shipped default) as configured and probes the credential, instead of reporting the shipped placeholder on every healthy install.
handfixes.why: press-traps section 5: doctorShippedBaseURL held a real single-endpoint vendor host (api.pax8.com was named in the fleet sweep), so doctor printed "ERROR base_url is still the shipped placeholder" and skipped the credential probe on every correctly configured install. The doctor-verdict replay restores doctor_verdict.go only when the reprint lacks it, so this edit survives onboard; a fleet re-mint of the doctor template would restore the placeholder value and fail this assert.

handfixes.summary: On an empty store every list the novel commands print under --json (since, overage, reconcile's two finding lists) is [], never null.
handfixes.why: press-traps section 3 (nil slices marshal as [], not null): an agent reads null as "no data was produced" rather than "nothing matched". The shipped novels declared the lists with var. TestNovelJSONListsAreArraysOnAnEmptyStore failed with one reverted (seen/novel-json-null).

handfixes.summary: The `company` novel and its `company show` leaf register with literal AddCommand, as the shipped tree did.
handfixes.why: press-traps section 3: dogfood's command walk follows only .AddCommand, so through 4.34.2's addNovelCommandIfAbsent the leaf `show` false-matched `profile show` and dogfood reported a command-depth mismatch. tools/apply_edits.py re-applies both lines after a render.

handfixes.summary: config.toml never holds a credential: every value it keeps passes persistedWithoutCredentials (base_url and token_url lose their userinfo and every credential-named or held query value; a credential-named header, or one repeating a configured or environment credential, is left out) and the write is refused when the file still repeats any held value; the legacy scrub writes through the same filter. The 0600 credential store is unchanged.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: `PAX8_BASE_URL='https://api.pax8.com/v1?api_key=X' auth set-token` wrote X (and a userinfo password, a held secret under any query name, a token_url query secret) into config.toml, because the generated save persists base_url and token_url as configured. Work order credential rule: nothing but the 0600 credential store holds a credential. Hand file internal/config/pax8_persist.go; three anchored lines in the generated config.go (tools/apply_credential_rules.py). TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential failed on the generated save (seen/r1-config-file-credential-seen-failing.log).

handfixes.summary: The chokepoint withholds a held value in every per-byte numeric encoding (quoted-printable with soft breaks, \x41, 0x41, %u0041, \u{41}, A, separated hex pairs, decimal, octal and binary byte lists), decoded as views of the text and of every view the funnel decodes, and in the fixed-alphabet and radix encodings the funnel does not decode (uuencode, xxencode, crypt and bcrypt base64, Crockford and z-base-32, RFC 1924 base85 and base45 at every alignment; base36, base58 and base62 whole), and the value reversed, case-folded, ROT13 and ROT47.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class secret-in-encoded-output: `PAX8_CLIENT_SECRET=ABCDEFGHabcdefgh12345678 pax8-pp-cli feedback '=41=42...' --agent` kept the quoted-printable secret in stdout and feedback.jsonl. The class is any text encoding the shared funnel does not decode, so families are closed, not names (hand file internal/cliutil/pax8_encodings.go, one line each in HeldEchoes and encodedCores). TestEveryByteEncodingOfAHeldValueIsWithheld failed on 24 encodings before (seen/r1-encoded-output-seen-failing.log), and on the families added while closing the class (seen/r1b-encoded-output-families, seen/r1b-encoded-output-forms).

handfixes.summary: A non-API request (feedback --send, a --deliver webhook) is refused when any held value can be reassembled from its parts in any order: userinfo, host labels, path segments, query names and values, fragment, header names and values, and the body's string values and words, each also decoded.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-split-across-outbound-parts: `PAX8_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT='http://127.0.0.1:9999/?a=<half1>&b=<half2>' feedback test --send` delivered both halves of the client secret: query names interrupted the joined views. Hand file internal/cliutil/pax8_outbound.go (outboundParts, coveredByParts). TestOutboundRefusesAHeldValueReassembledFromItsParts failed on all 10 shapes before (seen/r1-outbound-split-seen-failing.log).

handfixes.summary: The credential-name rule covers the standard auth carriers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, the authenticate headers, cookies, sessions, bearer and JWT values, signatures, assertions, SAML, one-time codes); a credential-named value's scheme-stripped and cookie-pair pieces are held; and a value shaped like a credential (Bearer token68, Basic base64 of user:password, a JWT) is held under any name. No Pax8 Partner API field name matches except provisioning key.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class holder-incomplete: a response member `"authorization":"Bearer X"` was neither held nor redacted, so X printed in successful output and the store. TestStandardAuthNamesAreCredentialNames and TestResponseCredentialUnderAnyAuthNameIsHeld failed before (seen/r1-holder-auth-names-seen-failing.log); TestNoPax8SpecNameReadsAsACredential keeps the rule from redacting Pax8 data.

handfixes.summary: The novels share one reading of each documented Pax8 shape (internal/cli/pax8_novel_rules.go): Subscription.status classified over the whole enum (Active, Activated, Trial bill; unknown statuses never count and are reported); Subscription.billingTerm (MRR is Monthly only; Annual, 2-Year, 3-Year reported beside it per term; One-Time, Activation, Trial excluded); one timestamp parser (numeric offsets with or without a colon; an unreadable date is never in a window); every collection read under the names sync and live reads store it as (usage summaries are the subscriptions_usage_summaries dependent); reconcile joins invoice lines to subscriptions by subscriptionId (a line for a period before a non-billing subscription ended is history; free trials, and in --draft mode non-monthly terms, are not expected on an invoice). After the Codex stop rule (unreviewed): a record stored under two names is read once, newest row first; a trial priced above zero bills; credit lines (InvoiceItem.type rebate, payment-credit, service-credit, invoice-credit, or a negative total) neither bill nor count as billed.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 wrong-result classes on documented shapes (spec.json Subscription.billingTerm and status, examples/subscription-history, UsageSummary as a subscription dependent, InvoiceItem.subscriptionId): One-Time charges counted as MRR; Activated subscriptions dropped; overage and company show read usage_summaries while sync writes subscriptions_usage_summaries (carried from 0.1.8); since dropped -0700 timestamps and kept unreadable ones; reconcile joined per company, so one invoice hid every other subscription's mismatch. Each test in internal/cli/pax8_novel_results_test.go failed before (seen/r1-billing-term, r1-billing-status, r1-unsynced-collection, r1-timestamp-format, r1-company-level-join, r1b-reconcile-expected-lines, r1b-reconcile-line-periods).

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
